recommendation: Keep the source fix as-is. Do not broaden this reconciliation into first/middle-name or v2 round-tripping guidance; FHIR-21226 records that such guidance belongs outside FHIR core.
issue_request: FHIR-16980 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core datatypes change request asking to clarify HumanName.given because 'full name' was ambiguous and the text did not explain whether multiple initials could be represented as separate given-name parts.
initial_application: The issue was initially applied by git-svn revision 14294, commit f1953dbb3236d9467f106f74e57d97607fd2a23c, which changed source/datatypes/humanname.xml. The element definition retained the approved clarification but included the typo 'paractical'; source/datatypes.html still carried parallel ambiguous narrative wording.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini actively lists HumanName under [types], and source/datatypes.html hosts the HumanName section with the datatype include, so both edited files are current build inputs. FHIR-21226 later asked broader v2/FHIR given-name mapping questions and was Resolved - No Change for FHIR core; community searches found no conflicting FHIR-16980-specific discussion.
reconciliation: Updated source/datatypes/humanname.xml to say 'practical limitations' and updated source/datatypes.html to say initials replace full name parts and may be separated into multiple given names, though often not due to practical limitations.
source_changes: source/datatypes/humanname.xml: corrected the FHIR-16980-applied HumanName.given comment from 'paractical limitations' to 'practical limitations'.
source/datatypes.html: aligned the HumanName narrative with FHIR-16980 by changing 'full name' to 'full name parts' and adding the approved multiple-initials/practical-limitations clarification.

related_jiras.note: Later same-topic question about given/middle/initials and v2 round-tripping was Resolved - No Change for FHIR core, confirming no broader core guidance belongs in this reconciliation.
